title: BACE: Safety & Workplace Culture - Biotechnology - SDS Reading
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: A technician accidentally splashes a chemical into their eyes. Which section of the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) should be consulted immediately for treatment instructions?
questions.explain: Section 4 of the SDS contains First-Aid Measures, which provide initial care instructions for untrained responders attending to an individual who has been exposed to the chemical.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: In the NFPA diamond rating system, a 'Red' rating of **4** indicates:
options: Material will not burn under typical fire conditions.
Material is a highly flammable gas or rapidly vaporizing liquid (Flash point < 73°F).
Material is unstable and may detonate.
questions.explain: On the NFPA flammability scale (Red), 0 is non-flammable and 4 is the highest hazard, indicating materials that vaporize completely at atmospheric pressure and normal temperature or are readily dispersed in air and burn readily (e.g., propane).
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: A 'Flash Point' listed in Section 9 (Physical and Chemical Properties) of an SDS refers to:
options: The temperature at which a liquid freezes.
The lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapor to ignite in air.
The temperature at which a solid melts.
The temperature at which a chemical spontaneously explodes.
questions.explain: Flash Point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid generates sufficient vapor to form an ignitable mixture with air near the surface of the liquid.
